questions.q: Why does Castlebridge Logistics pull its shipment record logic out into a child flow instead of building it inside both the warehouse flow and the finance flow?
options: Child flows run faster than logic built directly into a parent flow
So the logic exists in exactly one place and only needs to be fixed once
Because Power Automate does not allow the same action twice in one flow
Because child flows are required for every flow with more than five steps
questions.explain: The point of a child flow is reuse: one piece of shared logic lives in a single place, and any parent flow that needs it calls it, instead of duplicating (and later re-fixing) the same steps in multiple flows.

questions.q: What trigger must a flow use to be eligible to run as a child flow?
options: Manually trigger a flow
When a new item is created
Recurrence
When an HTTP request is received
questions.explain: A child flow must use the Manually trigger a flow trigger. That's what makes it eligible to appear in another flow's Run a Child Flow picker.

questions.q: How does a child flow send results back to the parent flow that called it?
options: It writes the results to a SharePoint list that the parent flow reads from
Through a Respond to a Power App or flow action (or the premium Response action)
The parent flow polls the child flow's run history
Outputs are passed automatically through a shared connection
questions.explain: A child flow ends with a Respond to a Power App or flow action (or the HTTP Response action on premium plans), which returns structured outputs the parent flow can reference in its later steps.

questions.q: Why does Castlebridge need to set each of the child flow's connections to "Use this connection" instead of leaving them as "Provided by run-only user"?
options: Because connections cannot currently be passed from a parent flow to a child flow at run time
Because run-only connections are always slower
Because only premium connectors support run-only users
It's a cosmetic setting with no functional effect
questions.explain: At this time, connections can't pass from parent to child. If the child flow uses anything beyond built-in actions or Dataverse, its connections must be embedded directly on the child flow, or the parent flow's call fails.

questions.q: Which flows appear in the Run a Child Flow action's picker inside a parent flow?
options: Every flow in the environment, regardless of trigger
Only flows owned by the same person building the parent flow
Only flows that use the manual trigger and live in the same solution
Only flows that have already run successfully at least once
questions.explain: The picker only lists flows that use the Manually trigger a flow trigger and are part of the same solution as the parent flow — which is also why Castlebridge builds both in the same solution from the start.
